name: Alt: three straight Vari desks, the four screens on 96" along the right wall, the 72" job desk on the left, no guest bed
notes:
Alternative for Andrew's office brief (2026-10-25: "multiple vari straight ones (bamboo), largest htat can fit"). The usable floor as in a and e: furniture from y 12 off the hatched heater wall (F-33, heater-depth-assumed), nothing in front of the wardrobe below y 116 or the door below y 122 (F-31: the 36" landings, assumed-position:closet and assumed-position:door). No desk stands along the window wall, so no screen faces the glass (F-38). Vari sells no bamboo top (vari.com's own search for "bamboo" finds nothing); every desk here is in Light Wood, its nearest finish, pale like bamboo.
The largest straight desks that fit: the right wall has 104" between the heater line and the wardrobe's landing (F-31), and two of Vari's 48" ComfortEdge desks fill 96" of it for the four screens (a 60" and a 48" reach 4" into the landing, and the 40x26 that would make 100" comes in no Light Wood); the left wall takes the 72" job desk, Vari's longest straight one. 168" of desk in all.
desk-1 and desk-2, Vari ComfortEdge 48x30, Light Wood/Slate: right wall, rot 90, x 76-106, y 12-60 and 60-108, the personal run. F-62 asks about 114" for four 32" screens flat (57" a desk); this wall stops at 96", so the four go on the HUANUO arms with the outer pair angled in about 38 degrees, about 100" across, overhanging the run's ends by about 2": it meets F-62 only on the arms, tighter than a's 102 3/8". F-33: 6" from the heater face; F-31: 8" above the wardrobe's landing and 14" above the door's (assumed-position:closet, assumed-position:door) · fits.
desk-3 Vari ComfortEdge 72x30, Light Wood/Slate: left wall, rot 270, x 0-30, y 12-84, the separate job station (the laptop on the ELLOVEN beside one 32" monitor, with room to spare, F-62); F-33 6" from the heater face · fits.
chair-1 FLINTAN at the run, x 46-74, y 48-76; chair-2 FLINTAN at the job desk, x 32-60, y 18-46, 12" from the heater face (F-33); 2" apart, and 46" between the two desks' fronts (F-35). To reach the job desk you pass chair-1: 16" with it pulled out, about 30" with it tucked under the run, as in a.
storage-1 BESTÅ shelf unit with door 23 5/8 x 16 1/2 x 25 1/4": left wall below the job desk, rot 270, x 0-16.5, y 88-111.6 (F-63), 59.5" clear in front of its door to the run (F-32); 25 1/4" tall, no anchoring needed. storage-2 BESTÅ shelf unit with doors 47 1/4" (top): hung above the job desk, underside about 74 3/8" up (the Vari rises to 50 1/2", so the job monitor needs it), its top about 89 3/8"; the ceiling is unmeasured (F-23; final audit 2026-10-26).
No guest bed: opened, the chair bed's foot would land under the run's desk-2, where its legs stand, and the job desk would have to shrink to 48" to give it the middle of desk-2; this layout keeps the larger desk. a, b, d and f keep the chair bed.
lamp-1 TÅGARP and plant-1 FEJKA: the bottom-left corner, left of the wardrobe's landing. lamp-2 RÖDFLIK (top) on the job desk's south end; lamp-3 RÖDFLIK (top) on the run's south end. art-1 PJÄTTERYD (top) over the low BESTÅ, from 54" up, one of the three canvases (a row of three centered on the BESTÅ would run over the job desk's south end, in its rising path); the other two hang on the right wall between desk-2 and the door, one above the other (final audit 2026-10-26).
rug-1 LOHALS (rug): x 28-80, y 22-99 (2" and 4" under the desks' fronts: level their feet). rug-2 Anji Mountain bamboo chair mat 60 x 48" (rug): x 29-77, y 17-77, across the aisle under both chairs, 1" under each desk's front, plastic-free in place of the KOLON (final audit 2026-10-26: the 48 x 42 lay under chair-1 alone).
The way in: from the door's landing into the 46" aisle between the run and the job desk, past the low BESTÅ (F-30).
Not placed: the chair bed (above); the KOLON (plastic; Andrew wants mats that aren't); the Vari 60x30 and 40x26 (rejected, above).
Kid safety (F-21): the job desk stands by the window and its chair rolls, so Maddie could climb to the window: fit window stops there (not in the catalog; the sill is unmeasured, F-38).
Vari's photos: allowed on 2026-10-26 (Andrew: "yes"); the three desks show their Light Wood photos.
Extras: the HOPPVALS blinds x2, two HUANUO dual arms (one per run desk), the FREIVID standing mat, the ELLOVEN, three FÖRSÄSONG cable trays (two under the run, one under the job desk, which had none until the final audit 2026-10-26), two BESTÅ rails.
Total $3,954.18, prices as of 2026-10-22 and 2026-10-23 and 2026-10-25 (those before today are price-stale, F-02). Flags across the layout: assumed-position:closet, assumed-position:door, heater-depth-assumed.
Final audit 2026-10-26, for every office layout: the HUANUO arms are C-clamps on the desks' back edges, and every run desk stands flush against its wall, so either the desk stands off the wall by the clamp's depth (not on the listing: measure the arm; at 2" the way in past the L's return becomes 31.8" in e and g, still over 30") or the arms use their grommet mount (the UPLIFT is configured with two grommets). No outlets are mapped: three motors, five screens, a PC and the lamps need a power strip in each cable tray (the MITTZON page offers KOPPLA, not captured) with a slack loop for the desk's 25" of travel, on the left wall or the right wall above the door. The wardrobe's left door, open 90°, stands on its hinge line at x 10, 1/2" from the TÅGARP and 1 1/2" from the plant's pot: fit a 90° stop on that door, and measure the room door's width and the wardrobe's distance from the right corner (the door as drawn, opened flat, lands 2" over the wardrobe's end). The way from the door to the job desk and the window passes the parked chair at the run (or the L) with 13 to 18 1/2" to spare, so the 30" walkway holds with the chairs pushed in.
